1: # OpenCL<sup>TM</sup> SDK (in development)
2: 
3: This is the Khronos OpenCL SDK. It brings together all the components needed to
4: develop OpenCL applications:
5: 
6: - OpenCL Headers (`external/OpenCL-Headers/`)
7: - OpenCL C++ bindings (`external/OpenCL-CLHPP/include`)
8: - OpenCL Loader (`external/OpenCL-ICD-Loader`)
9: - OpenCL utility library (`lib/include`)
10: 
11: It also contains resources useful to OpenCL developers:
12: 
13: - Code samples (`samples/`)
14: - Documentation (`docs/`)
15: 
16: ## Build Instructions
17: 
18: ### Dependencies
19: 
20: - This repository uses sub-modules for the OpenCL Headers, OpenCL C++ bindings, and OpenCL ICD Loader and some of their transitive dependencies.
21: 
22:   - To clone a new repository with all sub-modules included, use the `--recursive` option. Note that this option clones all sub-modules and their dependencies, which are not strictly required for the OpenCL SDK:
23: 
24:         git clone --recursive https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenCL-SDK.git
25: 
26:   - Alternatively, to clone only the sub-modules for the OpenCL SDK, first clone this repository without sub-modules included then setup submodules non-recursively:
27: 
28:         git clone https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenCL-SDK.git
29:         git submodule init
30:         git submodule update
31: 
32: - The SDK uses CMake for its build system.
33: If CMake is not provided by your build system or OS package manager, please consult the [CMake website](https://cmake.org).
34: 
35: - The SDK samples depend on
36: 
37:   - [Templatized C++ Command Line Parser Library](http://tclap.sourceforge.net/) (aka. TCLAP)
38:   - [Simple and Fast Multimedia Library](https://www.sfml-dev.org/) (aka. SFML)
39:   - [OpenGL Mathematics](https://glm.g-truc.net/0.9.9/index.html) (aka. GLM)
40: 
41: ### Example Build
42: 
43: In most cases, the following steps may be used to build the OpenCL SDK.
44: 
45: 1. Clone this repo and update submodules:
46: 
47:         git clone https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenCL-SDK.git
48:         git submodule init
49:         git submodule update
50: 
51: 2. Create a "build" directory:
52: 
53:         mkdir build
54:         cd build
55: 
56: 3. Generate build files inside of the "build" directory:
57: 
58:         cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
59: 
60: 4. Build the OpenCL SDK and copy files to an "install" directory:
61: 
62:         cmake --build . --target install --config Release
63: 
64:    Or, build the OpenCL SDK using the generated build files directly.
65: 
66: To customize a build, the following CMake variables are supported.
67: To specify one of these variables via the command line generator, use the CMake syntax `-D<variable>=<value>`.
68: See your CMake documentation for more details.
69: 
70: | Variable | Type | Description |
71: |:---------|:-----|:------------|
72: | CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE | STRING | Specifies the build type.  Does not affect multi-configuration generators, such as Visual Studio solution files.
73: | CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX | PATH | Install directory prefix.
74: | OPENCL_SDK_BUILD_UTILITY_LIBRARIES | BOOL | Enables building OpenCL SDK utility libraries.  Default: `TRUE`
75: | OPENCL_SDK_BUILD_SAMPLES | BOOL | Enables building OpenCL SDK samples.  Default: `TRUE`
76: | OPENCL_SDK_BUILD_OPENGL_SAMPLES | BOOL | Enables building OpenCL SDK samples that interoperate with OpenGL.  Default: `FALSE`
77: | OPENCL_SDK_BUILD_VULKAN_SAMPLES | BOOL | Enables building OpenCL SDK samples that interoperate with Vulkan.  Default: `FALSE`
78: | OPENCL_SDK_TEST_SAMPLES | BOOL | Enables a target to test the OpenCL SDK samples.  Default: `TRUE`
